profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC2 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

reading.body:
Equinix DC2 is a 118,446-square-foot single-story building in Ashburn, Virginia, with N+1 power and cooling redundancy and 30+ hours of generator autonomy at full load. The operator publishes no total megawatt capacity for this facility, only that cabinets support a minimum density of 4 kilowatts per rack, which means a fully populated building at this specification would draw roughly 29 megawatts assuming 7,200 racks and peak load—a calculation dependent on actual occupancy. The facility holds HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High certifications, qualifying it to host regulated workloads in healthcare, finance, and federal government.

DC2 sits in Ashburn's Data Center Alley, described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, anchored by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's own DC1 and DC2 buildings from the late 1990s. The site serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish megawatt figures; DC2 does not join that published set, so its rank cannot be determined independently of this calculation.

For AI infrastructure decisions, the critical gap is power capacity. Equinix publishes no megawatt rating for DC2, meaning this building's relevance to large-scale AI workload placement remains opaque from public data. The facility's age, peering-exchange heritage, and certification profile suggest it was built for enterprise colocation and internet exchange traffic, not the sustained high-density GPU compute that now drives data center growth. Without published power specifications, readers cannot assess whether DC2 can absorb modern AI training clusters or how it ranks against purpose-built hyperscale facilities.
